$comment: Single source of truth for the Separator API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: separator
title: Separator
description: A thin line that separates content, across or up and down.

decorative.description: Purely visual: hidden from screen readers.

label.description: A word in the middle of the line, like "or".

examples.title: Horizontal
examples.description: Between the parts of a card. A separator inside a card runs edge to edge.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.description: Between items in a row. It takes the height of the row.

examples.title: With a label
examples.description: A word in the middle, for choices like signing in with GitHub or with email.

a11y: An <hr> is a separator to screen readers, and aria-orientation says when it is vertical.
A separator that is only decoration should be hidden (decorative), so it isn't read between every item.
The labelled version is plain text between two lines, so the word ("or") is read.
